title: PRSS23 promotes pancreatic cancer progression through regulating Hippo-YAP activity.
authors: Liu, Zhihong; Jiang, Qiuping; Sun, Yuanmeng; Song, Yiran; Yu, Beibei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究PRSS23通过调控Hippo-YAP通路促进胰腺癌进展，核心是蛋白-蛋白互作与肿瘤机制，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by a poor prognosis, highlighting the critical need to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we demonstrate the pivotal oncogenic role of PRSS23 in PDAC pathogenesis. Clinical analyses reveal that PRSS23 is frequently overexpressed in PDAC tumor tissues, and elevated expression levels are significantly associated with reduced patient survival. Functional experiments show that PRSS23 knockdown markedly suppresses PDAC cell proliferation in vitro and inhibits tumor growth and metastasis in vivo. Transcriptomic profiling identifies the Hippo signaling pathway as a key downstream effector of PRSS23. Specifically, depletion of PRSS23 leads to inactivation of YAP, the central transcriptional co-activator of the Hippo pathway. Molecular docking simulations suggest that PRSS23 facilitates the formation of a ternary complex involving the serine/threonine phosphatase PP2A and the Hippo kinase MST1. Subsequent experimental validation confirms that PRSS23 silencing disrupts the interaction between PP2A and MST1, resulting in increased MST1 phosphorylation. This enhancement of MST1 activity promotes the phosphorylation and cytoplasmic sequestration of YAP, thereby suppressing its oncogenic transcriptional functions. Collectively, our findings establish PRSS23 as a novel prognostic biomarker and a crucial regulatory node in PDAC progression. PRSS23 drives tumorigenesis and metastasis by stabilizing the PP2A-MST1 interaction, which impairs Hippo pathway signaling and leads to aberrant YAP activation. Targeting the PRSS23/PP2A/MST1 axis may therefore represent a promising therapeutic strategy for the treatment of PDAC.
abstract_zh: 胰腺导管腺癌（pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC）仍是一种高度侵袭性的恶性肿瘤，预后较差，凸显了阐明其潜在分子机制的迫切需求。在本研究中，我们证明了PRSS23在PDAC发病机制中的关键致癌作用。临床分析显示，PRSS23在PDAC肿瘤组织中频繁过表达，且高表达水平与患者生存期缩短显著相关。功能实验表明，PRSS23敲低在体外显著抑制PDAC细胞增殖，并在体内抑制肿瘤生长和转移。转录组分析将Hippo信号通路确定为PRSS23的关键下游效应器。具体而言，PRSS23的缺失导致YAP（Hippo通路的核心转录共激活因子）失活。分子对接模拟提示，PRSS23促进丝氨酸/苏氨酸磷酸酶PP2A与Hippo激酶MST1形成三元复合物。随后的实验验证证实，PRSS23沉默破坏了PP2A与MST1之间的相互作用，导致MST1磷酸化增加。MST1活性的增强促进了YAP的磷酸化和细胞质滞留，从而抑制其致癌转录功能。总体而言，我们的研究结果确立了PRSS23作为PDAC进展中一种新型预后生物标志物和关键调控节点。PRSS23通过稳定PP2A-MST1相互作用驱动肿瘤发生和转移，该相互作用损害Hippo通路信号传导并导致YAP异常激活。因此，靶向PRSS23/PP2A/MST1轴可能代表一种有前景的PDAC治疗策略。
